config.title: React Router Basics

intro.title: React Router Basics
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple multi-page navigation app using React Router. You'll learn how to set up routes to display different components based on the URL path. The core concept is client-side routing, which allows navigation without full page reloads. You'll use key constructs like BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link. By the end, you'll have a functional app that switches between pages smoothly.
intro.usecase: React Router is the standard library for handling navigation in single-page applications (SPAs), enabling seamless transitions between different views without full page reloads. You'll use it to build product dashboards where users click between analytics, user management, and settings panels, or e-commerce sites where shoppers browse categories, view product details, and check out—all within the same app. As a developer, implementing React Router allows you to create clean, bookmarkable URLs and manage complex nested layouts, like admin interfaces with sidebars and modals, mirroring real-world apps from social media feeds to banking portals.

objectives: Configure a React application to use React Router for client-side navigation.
Implement a basic routing structure using BrowserRouter and Route components.
Construct a navigation menu with Link components to switch between views without page reloads.
Apply dynamic routing by extracting URL parameters to render specific content.
Initialize and render nested routes to organize complex page layouts.
Manipulate navigation programmatically using the useNavigate hook.
Integrate a 404 error page to handle unmatched routes gracefully.

steps.title: Import React and React Router DOM
steps.instruction: Import React from 'react' and import BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link from 'react-router-dom'.
steps.hint: Use import statements at the top of your file. Remember to import specific components from 'react-router-dom'.
steps.seedCode: // Import React and React Router DOM components here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary packages for React Router are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React is imported from 'react', and BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link are imported from 'react-router-dom'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've imported all the required components: React, BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link.
steps.feedbackWrong: import React from 'react' and BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link from 'react-router-dom'.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns JSX containing a <div> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a functional App component that returns an empty div.
successCriteria: The App component is defined and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named App that returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named App that returns a <div>.

steps.title: Wrap App with BrowserRouter
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, return a Router component (the BrowserRouter you imported as Router) that wraps the rest of your app content.
steps.hint: The Router component provides the routing context needed by Routes and Link components. Wrap your JSX with <Router> and </Router> tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component returns JSX wrapped in a Router component, establishing the routing context for the entire application.
successCriteria: The App component's return statement includes a Router component that wraps the existing div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the Router component wraps all the JSX content in the App component's return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Router component is missing or not properly wrapping the content. Remember to wrap your JSX with <Router> and </Router> tags.

steps.title: Create Home component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Home that returns a heading saying 'Home Page'.
steps.hint: Define a new function called Home that returns JSX with an <h2> element containing the text 'Home Page'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new Home component is defined that renders a heading with 'Home Page'.
successCriteria:
The Home component is created as a function that returns an

Home Page

element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Home component.
steps.feedbackPartial:
You've created a component, but check that it's named 'Home' and returns exactly

Home Page

.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Home component wasn't created correctly. Make sure to define a function named Home that returns the heading.

steps.title: Create About component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named About that returns a heading saying 'About Page'.
steps.hint: Define a new function called About that returns JSX with an <h2> element containing the text 'About Page'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new About component is created and ready to be used as a route.
successCriteria: The About component is defined, returns an <h2> element with the text 'About Page', and is placed after the Home component placeholder.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the About component, but make sure it returns an <h2> with the exact text 'About Page'.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The About component is not yet correctly defined. Create a function named About that returns

About Page

.

steps.title: Add Routes container
steps.instruction: Inside your App component's return statement, add a <Routes> component after the existing <h1> element.
steps.hint: The <Routes> component from react-router-dom will wrap your route definitions. Place it as a sibling element after the <h1>.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your App component will now have a <Routes> container ready to hold route definitions.
successCriteria: The App component returns a <div> containing an <h1> followed by a <Routes> component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the <Routes> component inside the App's return statement, after the <h1>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Routes component is missing. Add <Routes> inside the App component's return statement.

steps.title: Define Home route
steps.instruction: Inside the Routes component, add a Route component with path='/' that renders the Home component.
steps.hint: Use the Route component from react-router-dom. Set its path prop to '/' and its element prop to <Home />.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: mapping a path to a component
<Routes>
  <Route path="/" element={<Home />} />
</Routes>
steps.expectedOutcome: The Home component will be rendered when the user visits the root URL ('/').
successCriteria: A Route component with path='/' and element={<Home />} is added inside the Routes component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the Route has both path='/' and element={<Home />}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Route for the Home component is missing or incorrect. Check the path and element props.

steps.title: Define About route
steps.instruction: Inside the Routes container, add a Route component with path='/about' that renders the About component.
steps.hint: Add another Route component below the existing Home route. Use the same pattern but with the About component.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: another route with different path
<Route path='/contact' element={<Contact />} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The About component will be accessible at the '/about' URL path.
successCriteria: A Route component with path='/about' and element={<About />} is added inside the Routes container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a Route, but check the path or element attribute. Make sure it matches '/about' and uses the About component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The About route is not correctly defined. Add a Route component inside Routes with path='/about' and element={<About />}.

steps.title: Add navigation links
steps.instruction: Add a <nav> element with two Link components inside the div, just above the <Routes>. The first Link should have to='/' and text 'Home'. The second Link should have to='/about' and text 'About'.
steps.hint: Place the <nav> element as a sibling before <Routes> within the same div. Use the Link component imported from 'react-router-dom' with the 'to' prop.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: navigation with Link components
<nav>
  <Link to='/'>Home</Link>
  <Link to='/about'>About</Link>
</nav>
steps.expectedOutcome: A navigation bar with 'Home' and 'About' links appears above the routes, allowing users to navigate between pages.
successCriteria: The App component includes a <nav> element with two Link components: one to '/' with text 'Home' and one to '/about' with text 'About'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have a <nav> element containing two Link components with the correct 'to' props and text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation links are missing or incorrect. Add a <nav> element with two Link components: one to '/' (text 'Home') and one to '/about' (text 'About').

steps.title: Test the routing
steps.instruction: Click the Home and About links in your app to verify navigation works correctly.
steps.hint: Click each link and observe that the page content changes between the Home and About components.
steps.analogousExample:
// Testing navigation in a React Router app
// After clicking links, the URL and displayed content should update.
steps.expectedOutcome: When you click the Home link, the Home Page heading appears; when you click the About link, the About Page heading appears.
successCriteria: Navigation between Home and About pages works correctly via the links.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Make sure you click both links and verify the content changes. If it doesn't work, check that your links are correctly placed and the routes are defined.
steps.feedbackWrong: The routing doesn't seem to be working. Ensure you have both links and routes set up correctly, then try clicking them again.
